text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. Most APIs work over HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to send and receive data. The data usually comes back in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can use an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. APIs also have rate limits, which means you can only make a certain number of requests in a given time. Therefore, good error handling is important so your application can respond gracefully when something goes wrong.
